caller_census.method: whole-.text scan for E8 calls, E9 tail jumps and RIP-relative LEA references landing on the target, validated by decoding forward from the enclosing FDE start with Capstone (census.py). A site counts only on a real instruction boundary with the expected mnemonic.
notes: InitCompression 0x5f01e80: exactly 3 direct calls. Two inside rocksdb::log::Reader::ReadRecord 0x5f01f10..0x5f0294c, at 0x5f023c4 and 0x5f0286b -- the compiler duplicated the kSetCompressionType arm; both sites build the record identically (type byte at rsp+0x37, zeroed 16-byte Status slot at rsp+0x50, lea 0x37(%rsp),%rsi, this in rbx/rdi). One inside rocksdb::log::FragmentBufferedReader::ReadRecord 0x5f02f20..0x5f034f2, at 0x5f033ac (record at rsp+0x23, zeroed 16-byte slot at rsp+0x40). No tail jumps, no LEA refs.

Upstream shows one InitCompression call per ReadRecord variant; the binary duplicates Reader's arm. The dispatch reason (loop head vs back-edge, or jump-table sharing) was not traced and is recorded as an unknown.

No other caller exists in the binary: the routine runs when a kSetCompressionType record is decoded, which the caller only does once per log (a second record is reported as corruption but still processed, so the re-entry branches are modelled but not observed live).

cases.split: 600 type_install (all 256 type bytes twice with old uncompress_/buffer variation, plus the 10 named CompressionType values) + 600 create_buffer (10 named types x old buffer null/present x old uncompress_ null/present) + 600 reentry (two sequential calls, 10 x 10 named-type pairs) + 600 bindings (body/source hashes, 3 relocation displacements, 3 caller sites, 24 Reader layout fields, 8 constants, 8 upstream anchors, 256 type->product rows, 67 stride-1 16-byte windows, 75 8-byte windows, 72 4-byte windows, 82 single-byte rows over the 82-byte FDE)
what_is_checked: type-install: every type byte is read from the record's first byte, the flag is set before the type is stored (binary order), record_read_after is always true, and there is no early return for type 0 (the buffer is allocated and the flag set even when the product is null)

create-buffer: the Create call is (type, version 2, max_len 0x8000) for every type; the product is non-null only for type 7 (kZSTD) and null for the other 255 type bytes (including 0x40 kZSTDNotFinalCompression); the buffer is always 0x8000 bytes; a present old buffer is delete[]'d and a present old uncompress_ is leaked (overwritten without a delete)

re-entry: a second call leaks the first product, frees the first buffer, and installs a fresh product/buffer; a second call with a non-ZSTD type nulls the product while keeping the flag set and the buffer allocated

bindings: the body/source hashes are recomputed from the live binary and the census relocations; the 3 relocation displacements resolve to StreamingUncompress::Create, PLT operator new[] and PLT operator delete[]; the 3 caller sites are the census-validated sites; the 24 Reader layout fields pin the four observed offsets (+0x72/+0x73/+0x78/+0x80) and derive the rest from db/log_reader.h; every byte of the 82-byte FDE is covered by stride-1 windows and single-byte rows

0x5f01e80.model: 82-byte void InitCompression(const CompressionTypeRecord&) (Reader* in rdi, record* in rsi): movzbl (%rsi),%edi reads the type; movb $1,0x73(%rbx) sets compression_type_record_read_ BEFORE mov %dil,0x72(%rbx) stores compression_type_; StreamingUncompress::Create(type, version 2, kBlockSize 0x8000) at 0x61c1ce0 (kind-7 gate, null for any other kind, unchecked); mov %rax,0x78(%rbx) installs uncompress_ (old value overwritten without a delete -- leak on re-entry); operator new[](0x8000) allocates the fresh buffer (unchecked); the old buffer at +0x80 is loaded, the fresh one stored, then the old one delete[]'d when non-null via a tail jump; pop %rbx; ret. No kNoCompression gate, no .cold pad of its own.

observations: Flag-before-type: the binary stores compression_type_record_read_ (0x5f01e90) before compression_type_ (0x5f01e99), the opposite order to the upstream source listing (log_reader.cc:1129-1131) -- a code-generation reorder with no observable difference on a single thread, since both stores complete before the Create call.

Null product is a live path, not a crash: for any type other than kZSTD the factory returns null, upstream's assert(uncompress_ != nullptr) is compiled out, and the Reader keeps reading with uncompress_ == nullptr. A WAL advertising e.g. kSnappyCompression (1) or kZSTDNotFinalCompression (0x40) is read as if uncompressed; upstream's ReadPhysicalRecord branches on !uncompress_ for exactly this case.

Re-entry leaks the old uncompressor but frees the old buffer: a second kSetCompressionType record (which the caller reports as corruption but still processes) overwrites uncompress_ without deleting it, while the old buffer IS delete[]'d. The asymmetry is in the binary: the product install is a plain store, the buffer swap has the explicit null-tested delete.
Store-before-free: the fresh buffer lands in the slot (0x5f01eb7) before the old buffer's delete runs (tail jump at 0x5f01ec4), so the swap never leaves the slot dangling.

No kNoCompression gate: unlike the writer twin (which returns early for type 0), this routine has no early return -- even a type-0 record sets the flag, stores the type, installs a null product, and allocates the 0x8000-byte buffer. The gate lives in the caller, which only calls it after a successful DecodeFrom.
Live engine check: a real DCtx created through the system libzstd resets with directive 1 (ZSTD_reset_session_only, the reset the installed product's Reset performs); the reset returns 0.
